Figure 9: Token attention-survival under full-cache inference. Top row: Qwen3-4B on 100 OpenR1Math prefills up to T = 16,384 tokens. Bottom row: Qwen3-VL-4B on 98 MMDU multimodal dialogues (text + interleaved images), prefilled to the same length. Left column: survival rate averaged across all layers and query heads. Right column: survival rate for a single representative head (Math: layer 12, head 17; MMDU: layer 15, head 24). For each query position p we identify the head’s selected set of past tokens using either the top-K logits (K ∈ 64, 128, 256, 512) or the smallest set whose softmax mass reaches a threshold τ ∈ 0.90, 0.95, 0.99; a token of birth time i is then alive at horizon L if it appears in the selected set of some query at position p ≥ i + L. The dashed vertical line marks L = 4096. In every panel, every fixed top-K curve drops sharply with L, while the more lenient mass criteria stay substantially higher: the gap between top-K and τ-mass curves is the attention-dilution mass — tokens that still carry meaningful aggregate weight but are pushed out of the head’s hard top-K budget. Heterogeneity at the head level is large: a representative head on either dataset loses the majority of tokens by L = 4096 even under the most lenient criterion (99% mass), in contrast to the across-head average. The same qualitative shape appears in the multimodal setting (rows c, d), confirming that attention dilution is not specific to text-only inputs.

Figure 3: Prefill/compression with our method. A per-layer, per-head retention gate assigns each text/visual token a scalar score; the gate’s final projection is tied across layers to normalize scores. Tokens from all layers, heads, and modalities are then pooled and globally ranked by retention, replacing fixed per-layer/per-head KV budgets.

Figure 8: Empirical evidence for Assumption A.1. We extract the per-token query state qt at layer 20, head 0 of Qwen3-8B for 128 rollouts each on 10 AIME-24 prompts, project onto the top-8 PCA directions of the pooled training queries to obtain rt ∈ R8, and fit a per-context VAR(1) model rt+1 = Art + b+ ηt on 75% of rollouts. (a) Stability. Eigenvalues of A across all 10 contexts (each context contributes 8 eigenvalues) lie strictly inside the unit circle; the median spectral radius is ρ̃ = 0.76 and every fitted context is stable, so the chain is mean-reverting. (b) Mean reversion / ergodicity. For one context, the per-rollout running mean 1 t ∑︀ s ≤ trs[0] (grey) and its ensemble average (black) converge to the fitted µ (red dashed) inside a ±σ stationary band; the time average matches the ensemble average, consistent with ergodicity. (c) Sub-exponential innovations. Pooled log-survival of the whitened innovation magnitude |η| (blue) sits strictly between the Gaussian (red dashed) and exponential (green dotted) reference curves, satisfying the sub-exponential tail condition that drives the persistence bound.
